cases.name: Julie Ladd
cases.narrative:
She encountered Bell in the basement of her dormitory
at about 1:30 a.m. after she went down to do her laundry that day. Prosecutors at the time said she interrupted him as he was trying to steal money from the coin-operated machines.
He stabbed her to death with a boning knife when she fought his rape attempts, according to The Eagle’s news archives. Afterward, he sexually assaulted her dead body, prosecutors
contended at his trial and sentencing. Her body was found at approximately noon that day. There were parallel cuts running vertically from the top of her breastbone to approximately two inches below it. One of these wounds was not deep, but the other was approximately four and one-half inches deep. There were four parallel cuts down the cartilage and ribs around her breastbone, and her heart was penetrated in two separate areas. The post-mortem examination also disclosed evidence of post-mortem stretching of the lining of the vagina, which, in the coroner's opinion, would have been caused by penetration by a finger, sexual organ, or other blunt object, after death.

"Kristin's Law" is named after a woman shot and killed by her husband in Derby last year after a history of domestic abuse. Kristin Florio died in October of 2018 after a murder-suicide at the hands of Randy Gile. He killed her after he was released from jail, but Florio thought he was still behind bars for attacking her and making threats. The law will require victims of domestic violence to be notified if their accused attacker is released from jail.

cases.narrative:
ON 5/30/2023, 911 dispatchers received a call from Devin Nicholas Joel. He told dispatchers that he was attempting to kill his mother at a residence in the 5700 block of E Central. The dispatcher could hear a woman crying and screaming in the background. During the call, Devin made multiple disturbing statements about what he had done and intended to do to his mother.
‎ 
Devin reportedly captured photos and a video of Kacy, uploading them to SnapChat. He also FaceTimed his sister, showing her their injured and bloodied mother. When police arrived, they found Kacy in the backyard, covered in blood. She was transported to the hospital in critical condition, where she was pronounced dead at 6:15 PM. An autopsy revealed that Kacy died from a combination of blunt-force trauma & sharp-force injuries, including skull fractures and multiple lacerations.

cases.name: Mariana Nicole "Mari" Christian
cases.about:
KSN talked to some of her friends about the light she brought to their lives. A small but power-packed dynamite who loved hard, that’s the way friends describe 31-year-old Mariana Christian. Mariana’s friends say she was a positive light taken too soon.

“Everybody really, they really loved her more than anything else, and so for someone to do this is it’s unfathomable,” said Jenna Powers, Mariana’s Life Group mentor. Mariana Christian is a woman who practiced what she preached. In the wake of Tuesday’s discovery, friends say the loss is deeply personal.

“She was such a small person, but she was dynamite and power-packed, and she was so loving and caring,” said Powers.

Other friends like Stella Maxwell say Mariana was like her little sister.

“I am also from Romania, and she immediately got gravitated towards me because she is from there,” said Maxwell.

Maxwell says Mariana had so much she wanted to accomplish, like reconnecting with her biological family for the first time in 31 years.

Before his sentencing on Monday, the judge gave Mariana's family and friends a chance to talk about her and who she was. Her mentor, Deborah Matthew, said she came to love Christian like a daughter.

"I shared her hopes and that special someone, getting married, having children, and buying her first home," said Matthew. "Her senseless murder stole all that and so much more."

They say Christian had a traumatic upbringing and was previously homeless, but had found her way out of it and was now helping others through rides to work and food assistance. Matthew's Husband and another mentor to Christian, John Matthew, says Christian was helping Bearden when he killed her.

"He took advantage of her kind heart while she was just trying to help him get back on his feet. He stole everything he could from her apartment, even after he killed her," said John.

Zebib Christian, Christian's sister, called her sister a kind heart who her family was proud of.

cases.name: Naomi Oglesby
cases.about:
Family remembered Naomi Oglesby, the youngest of three sisters, as hard-headed, a jokester and someone who overcame a great deal in a short amount of time.

“She was happy,” (her sister Ashley) Stewart said of her sister. ”She always looked on the bright side of things.” She had long worked in the food industry, but took online courses and was saving up to take a certified nursing assistant test, Stewart said.

Naomi Oglesby spent her early years in south Texas. She and her sisters were often outdoors, fishing and hunting, with her stepfather, her sisters’ father, John Pape. Pape was in the U.S. Navy there before being transferred to McConnell Air Force Base. They moved to Derby when Oglesby was around 10. He continued hunting and fishing. The girls often went too. While her sister Christina Pape eventually picked up a gun to hunt too, Oglesby just went and helped retrieve. Pape said Oglesby was an expert at finding downed doves, rarely ever losing one.

“She was a big animal lover,” Stewart said, adding she had two cats, one named Bubbles and the other Butters, who have now been adopted by her friends.

cases.name: Daisy Aracely Valenzuela
cases.about:
Her obituary said: "Daisy lived a life marked by love, honesty, laughter, and a deep desire to care for others. She had a gift for making others feel seen and understood, and she carried herself with a bold and genuine presence that left a lasting impression on everyone who knew her. She was funny, spirited, and loving, and she brought energy and warmth into every room she entered.

Daisy attended school through the 12th grade and later pursued her calling as a nursing student. Her heart for helping people was one of the defining parts of her life. She was drawn to caring for others and had a natural compassion that made her well suited for a future in nursing. Her desire to serve was matched by her strong personality and her straightforward way of speaking. She was known as someone who had no filter and who did not pretend to be anything other than herself. Those who loved her appreciated her honesty and her humor.

She also enjoyed the lighter and more joyful moments in life. Daisy loved to party and knew how to have a good time with the people closest to her. She took pride in doing her makeup and hair, and she enjoyed being admired and feeling beautiful. She especially loved it when her cousins played with her hair, a small but meaningful expression of affection that brought her happiness. These simple moments reflected the tender and playful side of her personality, and they remain cherished memories for her family and friends."
